spec.title: vscode PROP-004: Build and test - install, hygiene, watch channels, runners, packaging stamps

status.comment: the type's answer to the build-and-test question of PROP-016 §2; the anchored facts moved verbatim from modules/codkit/PROP-010 in the split of 2026-09-09

p.VSCODE-BUILD-STEPS: The commands the universal `ci --profile build` skeleton calls for this type (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-011#PROFILE-BUILD`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-CI-IMPL`): the dependency install is `npm ci` of the tree and of `build/` (in CI it is supplied out of band and only its receipts are probed); the hygiene script is `npm run hygiene` and the lint script is `npm run eslint`, and both run **before** the overlay targets are materialized, because upstream hygiene is strict about the manifest it checks; the product and contract tests are `npm run test-node -- --runGlob vs/<ownRoot leaf>/**/test/{common,node}/**/*.test.js`; the package build is the upstream `gulp vscode-*` task. The order of the steps, the profiles and the exit codes are the engine's; the names of the scripts are this type's answer.

p.VSCODE-DEPENDENCY-ROOTS: **The dependency roots of this family are two**: `node_modules/` of the tree and `build/node_modules/` of the build toolchain, because the install of this distribution is two `npm ci` runs (##VSCODE-BUILD-STEPS). That is this type's answer to `build.dependencyRoots` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-DEPENDENCY-ROOTS`): a tree that restored only the first root is not ready for a build profile, and the run says which receipt is missing. The pair used to be a module constant of the engine; it moved here when a second family met it.

p.BUILD-COMMIT-COMES-FROM-THE-TREE-HEAD: **Build commit.** The product package build (`gulp vscode-*`) stamps `product.json.commit` from `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION`, and without it by reading `.git/HEAD` as a directory (`build/lib/git.ts` at pin 1.135.0); a managed tree is a linked worktree, its `.git` is a file, so the package is left without `commit`, and without `commit` the NLS loader does not read language packs. This is what `build.packageStamps` of this type answers - `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION` from the tree head and `VSCODE_QUALITY` from the quality channel of the patch set, or from the pin tag while it names none (##VSCODE-QUALITY-IS-A-PRODUCT-ANSWER) - and `codkit package` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE`) is the run that puts them into the environment of the packager. Codkit still neither writes the package nor changes code: it runs the upstream task and stamps what the task reads.

p.VSCODE-BUILD-CHANNELS-DEFAULT: **The default channels of this family are `transpile` and `typecheck`.** Its profile declares four; the other two compile the add-ons and are started by name when a change asks for them. This pair used to be a module constant of the watch wrapper and of the ci engine, which made it the default of every family (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-BUILD-CHANNELS`); it is this type's answer now.

p.VSCODE-QUALITY-IS-A-PRODUCT-ANSWER: **The quality channel is a property of the product, not of the pin it sits on**, so it is the patch set that answers it: `typeConfig.quality`, one of `stable`, `insider`, `exploration`, optional, and stamped into `VSCODE_QUALITY` as the literal word. A patch set that names none keeps the older answer, the tag of the pin - which is a version string (`1.135.0`), and therefore reads as "not the released channel" to every part of the upstream build that compares this variable with `stable`: the packaging of a bundled extension then takes its pre-release path, demands a publish counter it was never given, and the whole `codkit package` run stops. That is how this was measured, on the first real distributable of this family on 2026-09-09. Two things follow and both are recorded here rather than in the engine: the three words are the ones the upstream build itself distinguishes, so a fourth word is a `CK-E-CONFIG` refusal of the schema and never a value handed to a packager; and the operator keeps the last word anyway, because a stamp already exported into the environment is never overwritten (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-STAMPS-FILL-A-GAP`).

p.VSCODE-PACKAGE-SCRATCH: **The packaging of this family rewrites the manifest of a bundled add-on in place**, and a successful `codkit package` therefore used to end with a tracked file of the upstream changed: the add-on's own `package.json` gets its build kind, its version and its pre-release flag written by the bundler of the add-on, and the whole file reformatted. That is what `build.packageScratch` of this type names - `extensions/*/package.json`, the shape of those manifests rather than the name of one add-on, because which add-ons a distribution bundles is the distribution's business and not the type's - so `codkit package` puts them back and `status` calls what is left after an interrupted run packaging residue (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-SCRATCH`). Measured on 2026-09-09 on the first real distributable, where the run finished green and `codkit status` then advised extracting the bump into the delta. A quality channel of `stable` (##VSCODE-QUALITY-IS-A-PRODUCT-ANSWER) removes the version bump from that rewrite, because the pre-release path is what computes a new version - but not the rewrite itself, which is why the answer does not depend on the channel.

p.VSCODE-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS: **A raw bundle of this family is written beside the tree and names no output; an installer target writes inside the tree and names its outputs.** The `gulp vscode-*` task writes its result into a **sibling** directory of the managed tree whose name carries the platform and the architecture (`../VSCode-<platform>-<arch>*/`), while an output is tree-relative by contract (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-PACKAGE-ANSWERS`). Rather than widen the contract so the engine can list a directory it neither manages, guards nor cleans, this type answers with an empty `packageOutputs` and with no `outputs` for a raw bundle; `codkit package` then says that the type names no output, and the operator reads the location from the packager's own output, which the command printed in full. The Linux installer targets write under `.build/linux/` of the tree, and their outputs name exactly those paths (`##VSCODE-LINUX-INSTALLER-TARGETS`). For the same reason as before `build.packageDistributable` is empty here: the upstream tasks are the whole packaging of this family, and there is no second, product-supplied step after them.

p.VSCODE-PACKAGE-TARGET-CATALOG: The catalog is the seven raw bundles - `windows-x64`, `windows-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `linux-armhf`, `macos-x64`, `macos-arm64`, mapped one-to-one to the upstream `vscode-win32-*`, `vscode-linux-*` and `vscode-darwin-*` tasks - and the three Linux x64 installer targets `linux-x64-tar`, `linux-x64-deb` and `linux-x64-rpm` (`##VSCODE-LINUX-INSTALLER-TARGETS`); `typeConfig.packageTargets` may list these ten or the independent server target defined by `VSCODE-REH-LINUX-PACKAGE`. Windows hosts are measured for both Windows architectures. Every Linux recipe runs natively on a Linux host only: the raw `linux-x64` bundle a Windows host built carried Windows native modules, so it is refused on any other host with the way to the container named (`##DECISION-VSCODE-RAW-LINUX-BUNDLE-IS-LINUX-HOSTED`), and the three installer targets take the container route on Windows and macOS hosts (`##VSCODE-LINUX-CONTAINER-RECIPE`); the Linux ARM recipes have no container. Both Intel and Apple-Silicon macOS recipes remain macOS-hosted. There is no upstream universal-mac task. Signing, notarization, the Windows installers and `.snap` are not claimed by this catalog. Windows recipes resolve `signtool.exe` from PATH or the newest installed Windows 10 SDK before spawning gulp.

p.VSCODE-LINUX-INSTALLER-TARGETS: **Three Linux x64 targets carry what upstream's Linux build ships: the archive, the `.deb` and the `.rpm`.** Each begins with the upstream task of the raw bundle, `npm run gulp -- vscode-linux-x64`, which writes `../VSCode-linux-x64` - run by `bash -c` after the mirror of a provisioned Electron is up (`##VSCODE-LINUX-INPUTS`) - and goes on with what `build/azure-pipelines/linux/steps/product-build-linux-compile.yml` runs after the bundle at the pin 1.135.0; a line of that pipeline runs as `bash -c` with the line, in the tree. `linux-x64-tar` archives the bundle the way the step "Archive client" does: `.build/linux/client/code-${VSCODE_QUALITY}-x64-$(date +%s).tar.gz` (line 265), written by `tar -czf <archive> -C .. VSCode-linux-x64` (line 297), after the archives of an earlier run in that directory are removed; its output is `.build/linux/client/code-*-x64-*.tar.gz`. `linux-x64-deb` runs the upstream tasks `vscode-linux-x64-prepare-deb` and `vscode-linux-x64-build-deb` (lines 352 and 359) and then upstream's check that the data of the package is xz-compressed (lines 362-366, over the package where the task wrote it); its output is `.build/linux/deb/amd64/deb/*.deb`. `linux-x64-rpm` runs `vscode-linux-x64-prepare-rpm` with `VSCODE_SYSROOT_DIR` and `STRIP` set the way the step "Prepare rpm package" sets them (lines 381-383) and `vscode-linux-x64-build-rpm` (line 390); its output is `.build/linux/rpm/x86_64/*.rpm`. The dependency check of the two prepare tasks - `FAIL_BUILD_FOR_NEW_DEPENDENCIES`, `true` in `build/linux/dependencies-generator.ts` at the pin - is upstream's code and stays as it is: a bundle whose shared-library dependencies differ from `build/linux/debian/dep-lists.ts` or `build/linux/rpm/dep-lists.ts` fails its target. `VSCODE_SYSROOT_DIR` of the deb and rpm steps is the value an operator exported, and otherwise the client sysroot the tree already holds, `.build/sysroots/glibc-2.28-gcc-10.5.0`, which `build/azure-pipelines/linux/setup-env.sh` installs for the native modules: `prepare-deb` then finds the tarball it wants by its stamp instead of fetching the same one again into the temporary directory. The glibc check of the pipeline (lines 339-342) is upstream's `build/azure-pipelines/linux/verify-glibc-requirements.sh`, run as it is with its `EXPECTED_GLIBC_VERSION=2.28` and `EXPECTED_GLIBCXX_VERSION=3.4.25`, right after the bundle in each of the three targets and after the sysroot download of the same pipeline (lines 127-138), upstream's `getVSCodeSysroot`, which fetches nothing when the stamp of the sysroot is there; upstream points it at its server archive, which this catalog does not build, so the targets point it at the client bundle they ship, `SEARCH_PATH=../VSCode-linux-x64`, with the objdump of the sysroot of `VSCODE_SYSROOT_DIR` - and refuse when that objdump is not there, because the script reads the output of a missing objdump as no requirement at all and passes. Measured on 2026-09-24 on the bundle of the container: every ELF `.node` file of the bundle requires at most GLIBC 2.28.

p.VSCODE-LINUX-CONTAINER-RECIPE: **On a host that is not Linux the three installer targets are built in the Linux container of this type** (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE-CONTAINER`), whose recipe is `packages/type-vscode/container/linux/`: a `Dockerfile` and the entry it copies (`##VSCODE-LINUX-CONTAINER-ENTRY`). The container hosts are `win32` and `darwin`. The base is the public `ubuntu:22.04`, the operating system of upstream's Linux build pool (`1es-ubuntu-22.04-x64` in `build/azure-pipelines/product-build.yml`, `1es-vscode-oss-ubuntu-22.04-x64` in `.github/workflows/pr.yml`), never a private build image of Microsoft. glibc compatibility is not the image's: the entry runs upstream's `setup-env.sh`, which builds the native modules against upstream's glibc 2.28 sysroots, so the glibc of the image never reaches a package. Node is the version of the tree's `.nvmrc`, handed over as the build argument `NODE_VERSION` (`treeArguments`), from the official tarball checked against its `SHASUMS256.txt`, which is what upstream's `NodeTool@0` with `versionFilePath: .nvmrc` installs; `NODEJS_ORG_MIRROR`, the variable node-gyp and nvm read for the same downloads, names a mirror of `https://nodejs.org/dist` when the operator exported one. The packages are exactly upstream's prerequisites, with their sources: the list of the step "Setup system services" of `product-build-linux-compile.yml` - `pkg-config xvfb libgtk-3-0 libxkbfile-dev libkrb5-dev libgbm1 rpm bubblewrap socat`; the list of the step "Install build tools" of `.github/workflows/pr.yml`, upstream's own list for a stock Ubuntu runner - `build-essential pkg-config libx11-dev libx11-xcb-dev libxkbfile-dev libnotify-bin libkrb5-dev`; and the tools upstream's steps call that its build image carries - `curl` and `ca-certificates` (`setup-env.sh`, `build/linux/debian/calculate-deps.ts`, `build/linux/debian/install-sysroot.ts`), `python3` and `python-is-python3` (node-gyp, and `setup-env.sh` pipes into `python`), `git` (`build/npm/postinstall.ts` ends with `git config`), `fakeroot` and `dpkg-dev` (`build-deb` runs `fakeroot dpkg-deb`, `prepare-deb` runs Chromium's `dpkg-shlibdeps.pl` over the Dpkg perl modules), `file` (the deb check of the pipeline); `rsync` is the entry's own. They are installed with upstream's own `apt-get install -y`, recommended packages included. The image build receives `NODEJS_ORG_MIRROR` and the proxy variables (`buildEnvironment`: `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` and their lowercase forms); the container receives the proxy variables, `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY`, `npm_config_registry`, `NODEJS_ORG_MIRROR`, `ELECTRON_MIRROR` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the variables upstream's downloads read (`runEnvironment`).

p.VSCODE-LINUX-CONTAINER-ENTRY: **The entry builds in a copy of the tree the container owns, over Linux dependencies it installed the way upstream CI does** (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE-CONTAINER-PROTOCOL`). `HOME` and `TMPDIR` are directories of the volume, so the caches of npm, node-gyp and Electron and the downloaded sysroots live as long as the volume. (1) The copy is `/codkit/work/tree`, mirrored from `/codkit/tree` by `rsync --delete` with the modes `D755,F644` and without what an install or a build of the host wrote there, which is built for the host: every `node_modules/`, `/.build/`, `/out*/`, `/extensions/**/out/`, `/extensions/**/dist/`, `/.vscode/extensions/**/out/`, `/cli/target/`, `*.tsbuildinfo` and the `.git` of the tree - the host's native modules therefore never reach the build and nothing is written to the host tree; the paths of `executables` then get the mode 755 and those of `symlinks` become links again, and the copy is made a git work tree of its own, because upstream's install ends with `git config` in the tree it installs. That work tree has no commit, so upstream's `build-date-file` task (`build/lib/date.ts`), which writes the commit date of `HEAD` for a build that other machines reproduce, falls back to its other answer, the time of the build - each of the four container runs logged in full on 2026-09-24 printed git's `fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD'` for it; the version and the commit the package names are the stamps and are not affected. (2) The dependencies are keyed the way upstream keys its node_modules cache, by `build/azure-pipelines/common/computeNodeModulesCacheKey.ts linux x64 <arch of node>`: when the key the last install recorded in the volume is this one, nothing is installed; otherwise the entry runs the install of the pipeline in its order - `npm ci` in `build/`, then `setup-env.sh` (the sysroots and the toolchain), `node build/npm/preinstall.ts` and `npm ci` with `npm_config_arch=x64`, `VSCODE_ARCH=x64`, `ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1`, `PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1` and `ONNXRUNTIME_NODE_INSTALL=skip`, then `checkNativeOptionalDeps.ts` - and records the key only once all of it passed. An offline run installs nothing: when the key differs it stops before any build command, exit 3, saying that a run without `--ci` installs the dependencies into the volume of this tree. (3) Each provisioned tree input of `tree-inputs.json` replaces its cache in the copy, and the commands of `commands.json` run in the copy, in order. (4) Each output pattern is expanded as a shell glob in the copy, which reads it the way the engine does, and every match is copied to `/codkit/io/out` at the same relative path.

p.VSCODE-LINUX-INPUTS: **What the Linux targets download, and where a pre-provisioned copy goes** (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE-INPUTS`). Each of the three installer targets builds the bundle and checks its glibc first, which downloads three inputs: Electron, the version of `target` in the tree's `.npmrc`, which the bundle task downloads with `@electron/get` from `https://github.com/electron/electron/releases/download/` - `v<version>/electron-v<version>-linux-x64.zip` and `v<version>/SHASUMS256.txt` (`@electron/get` 5.0.0 keeps the archive in its cache but fetches `SHASUMS256.txt` on every run past it, so a warm cache still reaches the network: an offline run over a warm cache failed on that fetch with `EAI_AGAIN` on 2026-09-24), which is why the input is a mirror: `electron-mirror`, a directory laid out like those downloads (`v<version>/<file>`), handed to the bundle command as `CODKIT_ELECTRON_MIRROR_DIR` (`environment`), which serves it with a static server of node on the loopback for the run of the task, points `ELECTRON_MIRROR` - the variable `@electron/get` reads for its base address - at it, and takes the loopback out of any proxy, since the offline fence points the proxies at a closed port; the built-in extensions of `product.json`, which the packaging reads from `.build/builtInExtensions/<name>` when that holds the version the product names and otherwise fetches from their releases without keeping them (upstream's `npm run download-builtin-extensions` is what writes that directory) - the input `builtInExtensions`, which replaces that directory of the tree (`tree`); and the VS Code sysroot `x86_64-linux-gnu-glibc-2.28-gcc-10.5.0` from the releases of `microsoft/vscode-linux-build-agent`, found by `VSCODE_SYSROOT_DIR` with its `.stamp`, whose objdump the glibc check runs and which `prepare-deb` reads - the input `vscode-sysroot` (`environment`). `linux-x64-deb` adds what `prepare-deb` downloads: the Chromium sysroot that `build/linux/debian/install-sysroot.ts` keeps in the temporary directory under the name Electron's `sysroots.json` gives it, with its `.stamp` - the input `tmp`, a directory the commands get as `TMPDIR` holding that sysroot (`directory`); and the two files the upstream fetches with `curl` on every run, whatever is cached - Electron's `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v<version>/script/sysroots.json`, the input `sysroots.json`, and Chromium's `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chromium/chromium/<chromium version of cgmanifest.json>/third_party/dpkg-shlibdeps/dpkg-shlibdeps.pl`, the input `dpkg-shlibdeps.pl` (`fetch`). `build-deb`, `prepare-rpm` and `build-rpm` download nothing: the rpm dependencies come from the local `/usr/lib/rpm/find-requires`. The versions in the addresses are read from the tree, so a new pin names new inputs. In the container the Linux dependencies are the volume's own (`##VSCODE-LINUX-CONTAINER-ENTRY`) and are not inputs: an offline run needs an earlier online one to have installed them.

p.DECISION-VSCODE-RAW-LINUX-BUNDLE-IS-LINU:
**Decision:** the raw `linux-x64` bundle is built natively on a Linux host only; on any other host it is refused, and the refusal names the container route - the target `linux-x64-tar`, which builds the same bundle in the container of `packages/type-vscode/container/linux` and archives it - instead of building the bundle in that container.
**Why:** `codkit package linux-x64` on Windows used to run `gulp vscode-linux-x64` over the Windows dependencies of the tree, and the bundle it left carried Windows native modules - 19 of its 20 `.node` files began with `MZ` on 2026-09-24 - so the Linux application would not start and nothing warned. Building it in the container fixes the modules but not the bundle: the bundle is a directory of the host, and a directory of Linux files copied onto a Windows file system loses the modes a Linux application needs - the executable bits of the application and of `bin/`, the set-uid bit of `chrome-sandbox` - so what would land beside the tree would still not be a Linux bundle. The archive keeps them, and the installers carry the bundle inside them.
**Considered and rejected:** - building `linux-x64` in the container and copying the bundle out - a Linux bundle without its modes on a host that cannot hold them, and a directory beside the tree that the engine would have to write, which `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-007#CMD-PACKAGE-OUTPUTS-STAY-IN-THE-TREE` keeps out of its reach; - keeping the cross-build with a warning - the bundle is broken on every run, and a warning that always fires is not read; - installing Linux native modules into the Windows tree - they would replace the ones the Windows development build runs on.
**When to revisit:** if a host that is not Linux has to hand a raw Linux bundle to a later step that cannot take an archive - observed as a release step that unpacks `linux-x64-tar` by hand.

p.VSCODE-LINUX-INSTALLERS-NATIVE-PROOF: **Measured on Windows 11 with Docker Desktop on 2026-09-24**, by the opt-in proof `packages/type-vscode/test/linuxInstallers.proof.test.ts` (`CODKIT_LINUX_INSTALLERS_PROOF=1`) over a replica of the Nimbus patch set at `c86cb38` loaded onto the pin 1.135.0: `codkit package linux-x64-deb` and `codkit package linux-x64-rpm` took the container route and each left one artifact in the tree; apt installed the deb into a clean `ubuntu:22.04` and dnf the rpm into a clean `fedora:42`; `nimbus` resolved to a file of each package and printed `1.135.0` and the commit of the tree, the maintainer fields were the patch set's own, `/etc/apt/sources.list.d` and `/etc/yum.repos.d` gained nothing, and no installed script, desktop entry or AppStream file carried a CR. With the pin's Microsoft repository blocks put back into the replica's templates, the deb run failed on its new `vscode.sources` and the rpm run on its new `nimbus.repo`, every earlier check of both passing. The patch set alone builds `linux-x64-tar` and neither installer: `prepare-deb` requires the tunnel CLI `bin/nimbus-tunnel`, which the product does not build, and `prepare-rpm` finds five dependencies fewer than upstream's reference list, which upstream computes over a bundle that carries the tunnel CLI (`librt.so.1` and `GLIBC_2.5`, `GLIBC_2.27` of `libc` and `libm`); the replica carried two grafts of its own for them (`CK-build-901`, `CK-build-902`), which are not part of the patch set. Offline, `codkit --ci package linux-x64-tar` refused with `CK-E-NET-FORBIDDEN` before any write while its three inputs were missing, and with them provisioned built the archive in a container run with `--network none`.

tr.td: the only writer of JS into `out/`; on START it wipes `out/` (restart rarely and deliberately)
tsgo noEmit plus code generation into `src/`
40 projects; on start it wipes their `out/`
esbuild plus tsc noEmit of the copilot extension

p.DAEMON-TRAPS: Traps the wrapper implements: `npm run compile` and a restart of the transpile daemon wipe `out/`, so `build up` does not restart a living channel; before `npm install` in the tree the daemons must be stopped, so `build down --all` is invoked by the deps-advisory protocol; the upstream `watchd` scripts and our channels are mutually exclusive, so `up` refuses to start when a foreign watch process over the same tree is detected (probing by the command-line substrings `build/next/index.ts transpile --watch` and `gulp watch-`). On Windows the native process table carries parent pids, so the guard follows the complete available parent chain to a live identity-verified recorded daemon before classifying nested npm/cmd/compiler descendants as owned. A missing ancestor, a cycle, or an unrelated matching watcher remains foreign; POSIX process-group ownership is unchanged.

tr.td: `^Finished compilation with \d+ errors after \d+ ms$` (the counter is a 0/1 flag, not a number!)
`^(.+?)\((\d+),(\d+)\): error (TS\d+): (.+)$`; the real error count comes from `^Finished watch-client-noEmit .* with (\d+) errors\.$`
`^(?:\[\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\] )?Starting compilation$` (the optional `[HH:mm:ss] ` prefix is live watch output; the bare legacy form is accepted too)

`^(?:\[\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}\] )?(?!\[)(.+?)\((\d+),(\d+)\): error (TS\d+): (.+)$` (the lookahead forbids swallowing a broken prefix without a space into the file path). There is NO aggregate count line: the lines `Finished extensions <project> with N errors.` are the totals of individual projects, not the total of the pass, and are ignored deliberately; `errorCountLine` is empty, and the authoritative count of the pass is the number of parsed diagnostics (`countFromSummary: false`)
`\[watch\] build finished` / `Found (\d+) errors?\. Watching for file changes`

p.FALSE-END-GUARDS: `falseEndGuards`: the lines `Finished compilation <id> with … errors` with a non-empty `<id>` come from the code-generation channels (`api-proposal-names`, `extension-point-names`), which print their markers on every change; a naive match yields false pass ends. M1 refinement: with strict `passEnd` expressions the guards are defence in depth and become load-bearing only when `passEnd` is weakened; the count lines are separated into their own data field `errorCountLine` (for typecheck/copilot the count line is not a diagnostic; extensions has NO count field, and the authority there is the parsed diagnostics, REPAIR-003/006).

p.TESTS-LAYER-SPLIT: **The split by runners.** `--runGlob` bypasses the regular layer exclusion of the upstream node runner, and a suite that brings up the workbench pulls in style sheets that node does not load; therefore `ci --profile build` runs the node runner over the glob `vs/<own>/**/test/{common,node}/**/*.test.js`, while the `test/browser` suites of the product, of the library and of the features are a mandatory protocol step outside `ci`: the upstream electron runner (`scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/<own>/**/test/browser/**/*.test.js'`, under `xvfb-run` on a machine without a display), because a CI container without a display cannot make it mandatory for the profile.

p.VSCODE-REH-LINUX-PACKAGE: `server-linux-x64-tar` is an additional independent catalog target. It invokes the upstream `vscode-reh-linux-x64` task in the existing public Linux container route and archives the sibling `vscode-reh-linux-x64` into `.build/linux/server/vscode-server-*-x64-*.tar.gz`, retaining Linux modes. Node follows `remote/.npmrc` and the upstream Node checksum file, with built-in extension inputs declared separately; it does not substitute Electron client inputs, a model/account, authentication or an unpatched external server. Normal package drift guards, overlays, stamps and scratch restoration apply. Client target recipes remain unchanged. Actual server package/transport acceptance is required before reporting remote product behavior.
